daily_reality.summary: Hearing aid specialists (HIS) test hearing, select, fit, and adjust hearing aids for patients. They work in audiology offices, hearing aid retail stores, and healthcare facilities. Typical 40-hour week with patient appointments throughout the day.
typical_tasks: Administering hearing tests and interpreting audiogram results
Consulting with patients about hearing loss and treatment options
Taking ear impressions for custom hearing aids
Selecting appropriate hearing aid models based on patient needs and budget
Programming and fitting hearing aids using manufacturer software
Adjusting and fine-tuning hearing aids for optimal performance
Training patients on hearing aid use, care, and maintenance
Managing patient records and insurance documentation
Staying current with new hearing aid technology from manufacturers
key_documents: Audiogram results and hearing test reports
Patient hearing aid selection and fitting records

deadlines.hearing_aid_fitting: Typically 1-2 weeks from order to fitting
deadlines.trial_period: 30-60 day trial period required by most states
deadlines.license_renewal: Varies by state, typically annually or biennially

daily_reality.seasonality: Slight increase during fall/winter when holiday gatherings highlight hearing difficulties. OTC hearing aid market changes creating more year-round awareness.

regulatory.summary: State-licensed in most states with varying requirements. NBC-HIS voluntary national certification adds credibility. 2022 OTC hearing aid rule changed the market landscape. FDA oversight of hearing devices.

NBC-HIS certification optional but recommended (requires 2+ years dispensing experience)

regulatory.recent_changes: OTC hearing aid rule (2022) created a new market category for mild-moderate hearing loss, changing the competitive landscape. Some states updating licensing requirements in response. Growing scope overlap with audiologists.

terminology.summary: Audiology and hearing aid terminology combining medical, technical, and consumer-facing language.

terms.BC-HIS: Board Certified Hearing Instrument Specialist (NBC-HIS credential)
terms.audiogram: Graph showing hearing sensitivity at different frequencies
terms.pure-tone audiometry: Standard hearing test using tones at various frequencies and volumes
terms.sensorineural hearing loss: Hearing loss from inner ear or nerve damage (most common type)
terms.conductive hearing loss: Hearing loss from outer or middle ear problems
terms.dB HL: Decibels Hearing Level — unit measuring hearing sensitivity
terms.REM: Real-ear measurement — verification of hearing aid performance in ear
terms.gain: Amount of amplification provided by a hearing aid
terms.feedback: Whistling sound from hearing aid caused by sound leaking and re-amplifying
terms.OTC: Over-the-counter — hearing aids sold without professional fitting (FDA 2022 rule)
terms.BTE: Behind-the-ear — hearing aid style worn behind the ear
terms.earmold: Custom-made insert that directs sound from hearing aid into ear canal
terms.occlusion effect: Boomy sensation of own voice when ear canal is blocked
terms.telecoil: Hearing aid feature picking up electromagnetic signals from phone or loop system

career_psychology.summary: Rewarding patient-facing career helping people improve quality of life. Starting salary ~$50K, experienced specialists earn $60-80K+. OTC hearing aid market creating uncertainty. Strong patient relationships are key to success.
career_path: Apprenticeship with licensed hearing aid specialist (6 months-2 years) or associate's degree
Entry-level hearing aid specialist at retail or clinic
Gain 2+ years experience → pursue NBC-HIS (BC-HIS) certification

salary_range.commission_based: Many positions include commission on hearing aid sales

fears: OTC hearing aids reducing demand for professional fitting
Competition from audiologists with broader scope
Technology changing faster than skills can keep up
Patient dissatisfaction with hearing aid performance
motivation: Helping patients hear better and improve quality of life
Growing market due to aging population
burnout_factors: Sales pressure in retail hearing aid environments
Keeping up with rapidly changing technology

market.summary: Growing demand driven by aging population — 1 in 3 people over 65 have hearing loss. OTC hearing aids (2022) disrupted market but professional fitting still valued. Technology advances in Bluetooth and AI creating new opportunities.
